record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.context_brief: Complete solvability of 0-simple and Brandt classes
record.original_question: Determine whether the following classes are completely solvable, meaning that K(Φ) is recursive for every Birkhoff operator K: (1) finite 0-simple semigroups over groups lying in a pseudovariety of groups with decidable universal theory; and (2) finite Brandt semigroups under the analogous restriction on maximal subgroups.

evidence.quote:
Problem 4.2. (S.I. Kublanovsky)

     (1) Is the class of finite 0-simple semigroups over groups, belonging to a pseudovariety of groups
         with decidable universal theory, completely solvable?
     (2) The same question for the class of finite Brandt semigroups, under a similar restriction on
         maximal subgroups.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

(a) A finite semigroup S is called 0-simple if it has a zero element 0 and its only ideals are {0} and S, and S^2 ≠ {0}. By the Rees theorem, every finite 0-simple semigroup is isomorphic to a Rees matrix semigroup M^0(G; I, Λ; P) over a finite group G (the structure group) with a Λ × I sandwich matrix P having entries in G ∪ {0}. A finite Brandt semigroup is a finite 0-simple inverse semigroup; equivalently, it has the form B(G, n) where the sandwich matrix is the n × n identity matrix over G ∪ {0}.

(b) A pseudovariety of finite groups is a class of finite groups closed under taking finite direct products, subgroups, and homomorphic images. A pseudovariety H is said to have decidable universal theory if there is an algorithm that, given a universal first-order sentence φ in the language of groups, decides whether φ holds in every group of H.

(c) Let C be a class of finite semigroups closed under isomorphism. A Birkhoff operator is one of the standard class operators sending a class X of (finite) algebras to one of: H(X) (homomorphic images), S(X) (subalgebras), P_fin(X) (finite direct products), or any finite composition of such operators. Given a finite semigroup presentation Φ = ⟨A | R⟩, let K(Φ) denote the set of those finite semigroups in K that satisfy the relations R for some assignment of generators (equivalently, the membership/word problem associated with the operator class K applied to Φ). The class C is said to be completely solvable if for every Birkhoff operator K and every finite presentation Φ, the set K(Φ) is recursive (i.e., membership in K(C) is uniformly decidable from the presentation Φ).

Problem. Decide each of the following:

(1) Let H be a pseudovariety of finite groups with decidable universal theory, and let C_H be the class of finite 0-simple semigroups whose structure group lies in H. Is C_H completely solvable?

(2) Let H be a pseudovariety of finite groups with decidable universal theory, and let B_H be the class of finite Brandt semigroups whose maximal subgroups lie in H. Is B_H completely solvable?
